Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring licensed midwives to prepare written plans for each patient.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to written plans for midwifery; amending RCW18.50.010 and 18.50.108; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.50.010 and 1991 c 3 s 103 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Any person shall be regarded as practicing midwifery within themeaning of this chapter who shall render medical aid for a fee orcompensation to a woman during prenatal, intrapartum, and postpartumstages or who shall advertise as a midwife by signs, printed cards, orotherwise. Nothing shall be construed in this chapter to prohibitgratuitous services. ((It shall be the duty of a midwife to consultwith a physician whenever there are significant deviations from normalin either the mother or the infant.))

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.50.108 and 1981 c 53 s 14 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Every licensed midwife shall develop a written plan for((consultation with other health care providers, emergency transfer,transport of an infant to a newborn nursery or neonatal intensive care p. 1 HB 1130nursery, and transport of a woman to an appropriate obstetricaldepartment or patient care area. The written plan shall be submittedannually together with the license renewal fee to the department)) eachpatient following the initial patient assessment and before thecommencement of a regular program of midwifery services. The writtenplan shall describe the program of midwifery services to be provided;any general risk factors associated with the services to be provided;any specific risk factors pertaining to the individual health andcircumstances of the individual patient; a plan to be followed in theevent of an emergency, including a plan for transportation; andindividuals to contact in the event of an emergency. The patient and,if applicable, the patient's spouse or partner shall be informed of thecontents of the plan and provided the opportunity to amend any portionof the plan. Both the midwife and the patient shall acknowledge theirconsent to the contents of the plan before the continuation ofmidwifery services. The midwife must retain the written plans in thepatient's file for at least five years and make them available to thedepartment as necessary for credentialing and disciplinary purposes.The department may adopt rules to implement the requirements of thissection.
